[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Fargate profile uses this execution role, but it does not wait for the role's managed policies to be attached. The profile may become usable before its required pod-execution/CNI permissions are in place.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_eks_fargate_profile.this should depend on module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this. The profile references the execution role, but that alone does not ensure the required Fargate pod execution permissions are attached before the profile can be used to launch pods.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_eks_fargate_profile.this` references the pod execution role only through `pod_execution_role_arn` (a dependency on `module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_iam_role.this`), and never depends on `module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this`. The Fargate profile is submitted to EKS with that role before `AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy` and the CNI policy are attached to it, so profile creation can fail (the role is not yet authorized to run Fargate pods / manage ENIs) or pods scheduled to the profile cannot pull images or register. On destroy the reverse ordering is also unguarded. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this]` to `aws_eks_fargate_profile.this`; there is no attribute reference that can carry this ordering, since the attachment exposes no attributes the profile consumes.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_eks_fargate_profile.this only references the pod-execution IAM role (aws_iam_role.this[0].arn) and never the policy attachment. Unlike the node-group modules (which enforce this ordering through a launch template that carries depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this]), the Fargate module has no such path, so the profile can be created before the pod-execution role has AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy attached. IAM is eventually consistent, so Fargate pods scheduled right after will fail with authorization errors until the policy propagates. The profile should depend_on module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this (a bare depends_on is required — no attribute on the profile can reference the attachment to infer it implicitly).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The Fargate profile (aws_eks_fargate_profile.this) references only the bare pod-execution IAM role (pod_execution_role_arn) and — unlike the node-group modules, which have no launch template to transitively depend on the attachments — has no dependency at all on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this. The pod execution role needs AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy / CNI policy attached before Fargate pods can run, so the profile should be ordered after the attachments; nothing in the configuration expresses this.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The Fargate profile references the pod execution role via pod_execution_role_arn, but has no ordering against the role's policy attachments. Fargate profile creation is asynchronous: once the profile becomes ACTIVE, pods matching its selectors are scheduled immediately and must assume the role with AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy (and the CNI policy) already attached, otherwise those pods cannot run. An explicit depends_on on the policy attachment ensures the permissions exist before the profile goes ACTIVE.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_eks_fargate_profile.this references only the IAM role itself (pod_execution_role_arn = aws_iam_role.this[0].arn) but has no ordering guarantee against aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this, which attaches AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy (and the CNI policy). Unlike the node-group modules there is no launch template (or other resource) whose depends_on could indirectly establish this ordering, so the Fargate profile can be created while the pod execution role still has no permissions, causing pods scheduled onto Fargate to fail with Access Denied until propagation completes. This matches the module's own convention: the cluster and both launch templates explicitly gate on their role policy attachments. No data-reference fix applies since pod_execution_role_arn must reference the role, not the attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`aws_eks_fargate_profile.this` references the pod execution role via `pod_execution_role_arn = aws_iam_role.this[0].arn`, but has no ordering guarantee on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this`. Fargate profile creation is asynchronous and EKS requires the pod execution role to already carry its policies (AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy and the CNI policy); if the attachments land after the profile is created, pods scheduled on Fargate fail to launch (or profile creation fails) until the role propagates. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this]` (or an equivalent ordering) so the attachments are applied before the profile is registered with EKS. No clean data-reference fix exists since the profile only consumes the role ARN.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The EKS managed node group uses this IAM role but does not wait for its required managed policies to be attached. The AWS provider documentation specifically recommends this dependency so EKS can properly handle node instances and network interfaces.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_eks_node_group.this should depend on module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this so EKS role permissions are attached before node-group handling and remain attached until the node group is deleted. The provider documentation recommends this explicit ordering; the existing role ARN reference only orders the role itself.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
`module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_eks_node_group.this` should wait for `module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this` so EKS has the node-role permissions before creating or deleting the managed node group. The provider documentation specifically recommends this ordering; the launch-template dependency only covers cases where that template is actually created.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_eks_node_group.this` only orders against `module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role.this` (through `node_role_arn`); it has no dependency on `module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this`. The node role ARN exists before the AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy / AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly / CNI policies are attached to it, so Terraform may create the node group (and EKS start launching and joining instances) while the role is still permissionless, and on destroy the role can be stripped of permissions before EKS has finished terminating instances and ENIs. The AWS provider documentation for `aws_eks_node_group` explicitly recommends depending on the role policy attachments for exactly this reason. The launch template's own `depends_on` only covers the case where this module creates the launch template.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The EKS managed node group (aws_eks_node_group.this) only references the bare IAM role (node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.this[0].arn) and has no dependency on the role's policy attachments. Per the official aws_eks_node_group docs, the node group must be created after (and destroyed before) its AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy / AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly / CNI policy attachments exist, or nodes fail to register and EKS cannot cleanly delete instances and ENIs. No attribute reference or depends_on expresses this ordering.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The EKS managed node group references the node IAM role via node_role_arn, but has no ordering against the role's policy attachments (AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, CNI). Node group provisioning is asynchronous: instances are launched and attempt to join the cluster as soon as the node group is created, and they need those policies attached to the role. The aws_launch_template.this resource carries a depends_on for the attachments, which only covers the case where a custom launch template is created; when create_launch_template is false (or the module is otherwise reordered), nothing guarantees the attachments exist before nodes launch. The aws_eks_node_group documentation explicitly recommends depends_on on the role's policy attachments.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_eks_node_group.this references only the IAM role itself (node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.this[0].arn) but has no ordering guarantee against aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this. EKS node groups require AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy and AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly to be attached to the node role; because IAM policy attachment is eventually consistent, creating the node group concurrently with the attachments can leave nodes unable to join (or the API rejecting the role). The AWS provider docs explicitly recommend depends_on on the role policy attachments for aws_eks_node_group. In the default configuration the launch template's depends_on covers this indirectly, but when create_launch_template = false the EKS default launch template is used and no chain exists. Note: no data-reference fix is offered because node_role_arn must keep pointing at the role, not an attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`aws_eks_node_group.this` sets `node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.this[0].arn` but never waits for `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this`. The AWS provider docs explicitly require the node role's policies (AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly) to be created before and deleted after node group handling — otherwise EKS cannot properly register/delete instances and ENIs. The ordering is currently only covered transitively when a custom launch template is created (`aws_launch_template.this` depends_on the attachments); when `create_launch_template = false` the node group races the attachments with no guarantee. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this]` on the node group. No clean data-reference fix exists since the node group only consumes the role ARN.
